$comment: LP FIDELITY LEDGER. Each entry is a geometric quantity measured on real LilyPond,
paired with the difference Lily# currently shows. See README.md for how to add or
regenerate an entry. The 'lilypond' numbers are DATA: they change only by re-running
the probes in probes/ against lilypond.exe and pasting what it prints.
residual = lilysharp - lilypond, in staff-spaces. A non-zero residual MUST carry a
'why'. Naming the defect is the goal; where it is not yet isolated, say so with an
'OPEN:' prefix and state exactly what is unexplained. What is forbidden is a silent
baseline. Both directions of change are failures: a residual that grows is a
regression, and a residual that shrinks is progress that must be recorded on purpose
so it appears in the diff rather than being absorbed.
The count of exact entries and the total |residual| are the headline fidelity numbers.

barline.next.down-stems-after-clef.why: OPEN: appeared with the 2.26.0 font, and only its scale is accounted for. The quantity is 0.9 (next-note) plus the optical correction, and LilyPond's correction moved 0.189365 -> 0.189360 with that font's LILC rounding while Lily#'s stayed at 0.189365449. So the cause is the same rounding that moved the other nine measured values -- it is bounded by that rounding (<= 7e-5) and it arrived on the same commit -- but WHICH glyph metric carries the 5.4e-6 through Staff_spacing's /7 has not been isolated. Smallest residual in the corpus. The attribution is not settled.

barline.next.accidental-to-notehead.why: EXACT since LilyPond 2.26.0, and NOT because anything in Lily# changed. 2.26.0 rebuilt Emmentaler with the LILC bboxes rounded to three decimals in the design unit, which put accidentals.sharp's right edge on exactly 1.100000 (2.24.4: 1.100010). The skyline term that separated LilyPond's measurement from Lily#'s box measurement was -0.000010 and is now zero. The horizontal skyline is still not ported (accidental-placement.cc:412) -- this entry merely stopped being able to see it. barline.next.key-change-to-notehead is now the only entry that still measures it.

barline.next.key-change-to-notehead.why: The NATURAL's skyline term, arriving through Paper_column::minimum_distance exactly as the sharp's does in the two entries above — the note opening this measure is a c' under A major, so it carries one, and its reach is the musical column's leftmost ink. A natural is vertically thin, so its right skyline stands 0.017606 further out than its box (measured by zeroing AccidentalPlacement's two paddings on 2.24.4); a sharp's term is 0.000010, which is why this entry is the largest of the three. Same single cause. Was -2.234272 before the boundary column, -0.034272 before the padding.

barline.next.time-change-to-notehead.why: The TimeSignature grob's own width, and the SOURCE of the number is now located: ly:time-signature::print builds a MARKUP and hands it to grob-interpret-markup (scm/time-signature.scm:18-29), and markup text is measured by the text layout engine, not by the music-font path Lily# and the rest of this corpus use. Asked both ways on one and the same grob on 2.24.4: ly:font-get-glyph 'fattened.four' gives 1.600000 while (markup #:number "4") gives 1.604735. So Lily#'s 1.600000 is not a stale or wrong constant — it is exactly what LilyPond's own music-font path reports for that glyph; the two paths simply disagree. Ruled out as the source of 1.604735, for all ten digits: the LILC bbox, the raw outline bounds, the advance, the plain digit family at U+0030-0039 as well as fattened at U+E0B4-U+E0BF, and a font-build difference (LilyPond 2.24.4 ships a different-sized emmentaler-20.otf than the repo copy, but their digit metrics are identical). The markup widths group 0/2/8 at 1.468162, 3/5/7 at 1.331589 and 6/9 at 1.365732, a grouping no metric in the font file reproduces, and a two-digit string is not the concat of two one-digit widths (off by 0.102430 either way) — both consistent with a shaped text run. Closing this needs that text pipeline's metrics, not a constant. The 1.600000 rides through Staff_spacing untouched (the space-alist ideal binds here, not the 0.3 + min_dist correction), so the residual is exactly the width difference. Was -1.454735 before the boundary column existed.

midmeasure.key-cancel.key-to-next-note.why: EXACT since LilyPond 2.26.0, by the same rounding that closed barline.next.accidental-to-notehead: the sharp's skyline term went to zero. That the two closed together, both having read 0.000010, is what confirms the earlier reading that they were one cause and not two.

page.first-staff-refpoint.why: EXACT. LilyPond seats the first system with top-system-spacing's SPRING, and at force 0 a spring is max(min_distance, ideal_distance) (lily/spring.cc:219-237), so basic-distance 6 beats the ink floor -- ink above the refpoint (2.000000, the staff's own half height on this probe) plus padding 1 -- and the staff lands at top-margin + 6.000000 exactly. Lily# returned the floor alone and sat 3.000000 too high. Closing it took two steps IN ORDER, and the order is the finding: the placement had to move into the refpoint frame FIRST, because top-system-spacing aims at the staff's MIDDLE line while Lily# stacks systems by the top staff's TOP LINE. Porting the max() onto the unconverted anchor lands the top line on the value LilyPond puts the refpoint at -- measured 2026-07-22, that moves the residual -3.000000 -> +2.000000 rather than to 0. What this does NOT cover: the top spring's STRETCH under page justification (set_default_stretch_strength = ideal_distance, spring.cc:213-216). Lily# pins the first system and stretches only the inter-system springs; this probe is a natural-length page, so that difference cannot show here.

system.natural-distance.why: EXACT. system-system-spacing's basic-distance, 12, and the first Y quantity in this corpus to be confirmed rather than assumed: HANDOFF had it as 'a match' from an SVG reading at two decimals, which cannot tell 12.00 from 12.004. Measured through RecordingDocumentContext it is 12.000000 on both sides. Note what this does NOT cover: the probe is the LAST page of a score that fits one page, so the gap is the spring's natural length. The STRETCHED regime is now carried by system.stretched-distance.

page.stretched.first-staff-refpoint.why: Was -0.025482000 (seeded before the change, predicted exactly), closed to +0.000371455 by porting the chain. The remainder is NOT structural: it is the last-bottom spring's floor, and it is the same 0.044994 that system.stretched-distance carries -- see that entry. LilyPond builds ONE chain of springs per page -- top-system-spacing, one spring per system pair, then last-bottom-spacing -- and solves it against page_height_ = paper-height - top-margin - bottom-margin (page-layout-problem.cc:780-804, Simple_spacer). On a full page every spring in that chain carries the SAME force, so the top spring stretches too: measured on 2.26.0 the first refpoint sits at top-margin + 6.025482 rather than the natural 6.000000. The chain reproduces that to six digits from the source alone: (6 + 6f) + 12*(12 + 60f) + 4.544994 = 157.628268 gives f = 0.00424693, hence 6.025482 and 12.254816. The 4.544994 is last-bottom-spacing blocked at its own floor (padding 1 + 3.544994 of ink below the last refpoint). PREDICTION: Lily# currently pins the first system at its natural distance and stretches only the inter-system springs, so this should read 11.690551 (residual -0.025482) before the port and 11.716033 (residual 0) after.

system.stretched-distance.why: Was +0.089206333 before the chain was ported; the port took 96 percent of it. The remainder is ONE quantity, and it is not the spacing model: the ink hanging below the LAST system's refpoint reads 3.500000 in Lily# against 3.550000 in LilyPond. Everything else in the chain agrees to six digits. That 0.050000 was first mis-attributed here to half of LilyPond's staff-line thickness, from a figure (3.544994) that was arithmetic on a ROUNDED gap; reading the probe's raw per-system dump instead gives 3.550000000 exactly, on every system of both pages. The real cause is the notehead: the lowest note is c' with its head 3.000000 below the refpoint, so LilyPond's ink puts the head's half-height at 0.550000, while Lily# seeds its vertical skyline from EngravingDefaults.NoteheadHeight = 1.0, a nominal staff space. Lily# ALREADY has the true ink -- GlyphMetricsGenerated.NoteheadBlack is (-0.545000 .. 0.545000) from the LILC table -- so this is the vertical half of what ec7a2254 did for X, still not wired to the skyline. Fixing that accounts for 0.045000 of the 0.050000 and touches every vertical skyline, so it is its own island; the last 0.005000 (LilyPond 0.550000 against LILC's 0.545000) is NOT yet explained and must not be papered over. The system spring of the same chain as page.stretched.first-staff-refpoint, on the SAME page -- page 1 of book J, which is full. Uniform across all 12 gaps in LilyPond's dump. The predicted DIRECTION was right and the magnitude was not: Lily# solves its force over the inter-system springs ALONE (no top spring, no last-bottom spring in the chain), so the force comes out too large, but the guess of 'roughly 12.29' was copied from a stale HANDOFF figure rather than derived. Derived from Lily#'s own PASS 2 it is exact: it fills to the bottom margin with the last system's INK, leaving 4.128268 to share over 12 gaps at equal stretch = +0.344022 each, i.e. 12.344022. LilyPond instead gives that last spring last-bottom-spacing's floor (padding 1 + the ink) and lets it stretch (stretchability 30), and adds the top spring (inverse stretch 6) to the same chain. PREDICTION: 0 after porting the chain. Do NOT read this entry on the last page: ragged-last-bottom makes that page a fixed_force_solution of the PREVIOUS page's force, which is a different measurement (page-breaking.cc:565-575).

page.stretched.systems-on-first-page.why: MEASURED EXACT ON ARRIVAL, which is the finding: this probe does NOT catch the defect it was seeded for, and page.tight.* had to be built because of it. Everything else on this page describes how a page holding N systems is spaced; nothing has ever measured N. LilyPond prices a page against `page_height_ - min_whitespace_at_top_of_page(first) - min_whitespace_at_bottom_of_page(last)` (lily/page-spacing.cc:30-41), and those two terms are the page breaker's ONLY knowledge of the top-system and last-bottom springs. Each is `max(0, max(padding, minimum-distance -/+ translate))` (page-breaking.cc:1785-1823). On the shipping specs top-system-spacing and last-bottom-spacing both carry minimum-distance 0 and padding 1, and translate is the system's own up/down reach, so BOTH terms evaluate to exactly 1.000000 and LilyPond's usable band is 157.628268 - 2 = 155.628268. Lily#'s PageSpacing.CalcForce subtracts the MARGINS only, so it hands the breaker 157.628268 -- 2.000000 ss MORE room than LilyPond has. That is the whole of the divergence HANDOFF 2-8 records as `PageBreaker is out of sync with the chain`, expressed as a number for the first time. PREDICTION was: Lily# fits at least LilyPond's 13 and, if 2.000000 is enough for one more, 14 -- residual 0 or +1, never negative. MEASURED: 0. The prediction's bound held, and the answer is the uninteresting end of it: 2.000000 is not enough for a 14th system here. The reason turned out to be deeper than slack, and is worth keeping -- on default paper this count is not decided by capacity AT ALL. Raising the first system by up to four octaves (eight ledger steps, measured on 2.26.0) leaves LilyPond at 13 every time, so the breaker is choosing from the force each candidate page solves to, not from a rod hitting a ceiling. That is why this entry reads exact while the model behind it is wrong, and why page.tight.* had to shrink the paper before anything would bind. Keep it as the A4 control. LilyPond measured on 2.26.0: 13 on page 1, 8 on page 2.

page.stretched.page-count.why: The companion to page.stretched.systems-on-first-page: the per-page count alone cannot tell an over-filling breaker from one that simply paginates differently, because moving one system off page 1 and onto page 2 leaves the total unchanged. 21 systems at LilyPond's 13 + 8 fit two pages either way, so PREDICTION: 2, residual 0, BEFORE and AFTER the fix. An entry that is expected to stay green is worth having here precisely because it is the control -- if it ever moves, the change did something other than re-price the page, and the sibling entry alone could not tell me that.

page.tight.page-count.why: Now exact, and read together with page.tight.systems-on-first-page: at 70 staff spaces both sides take two pages and cut them 5 + 1. It was seeded at 72 where it read -1 (Lily# one page against LilyPond's two) and the three ports below closed that; the probe then moved to 70 because 72 became Lily#'s own flip point and the entry would have swung on unrelated changes. Re-measured 2026-07-22 with a one-line-per-BOOK dump after the earlier per-PAGE dump was found to be losing lines: LilyPond takes two pages for every height up to 75 and Lily# up to 76, so 70 sits five or six staff spaces inside BOTH plateaus. ⚠️ An earlier note here said LilyPond stayed at two pages through 77 and flipped at 79; that was read off truncated dumps and is WRONG. What actually happens at 76 and 77 is not a paging difference at all -- see page.tight.systems-on-first-page. History and model follow. Six systems on 72-staff-space paper: LilyPond takes two pages for every height from 69 to 77 and only reaches one at 79. Lily# reaches one page at 71 -- SEVEN staff spaces early -- so at 72 it prints one page where LilyPond prints two. Three LP-sourced divergences in the breaker, all measured: (1) constrained-breaking.cc:555 sets `inverse_hooke_ = full_height() + system_system_space_` = 7.35 + 12 = 19.35 per line, while Lily# uses `max(0.1, Stretchability/60)` = 1.0 -- a factor of 19 in the force denominator, and NOT the same formula at all (the breaker does not use stretchability). This is the /60 transcription cfdf85b4 abolished in the placement chain, still alive in the breaker. (2) page-spacing.cc:30-41 prices the page against `page_height_ - min_whitespace_at_top_of_page(first) - min_whitespace_at_bottom_of_page(last)`; each is `max(0, max(padding, minimum-distance -/+ translate))` (page-breaking.cc:1785-1823) and on the shipping specs both come to exactly 1.000000, so Lily# hands the breaker 2.000000 ss too much. (3) LilyPond's `bottom_padding_` is only ever assigned 0 (constrained-breaking.cc:621) so its term is inert, while Lily# subtracts the system's padding 1.000000 there. PREDICTION: 2 after all three are ported. If it lands on 2 with only some of them, the rest are still wrong and the entry is passing by cancellation -- page.tight.systems-on-first-page is the cross-check.

page.tight.systems-on-first-page.why: Closed. LilyPond puts 5 systems on page 1 and 1 on page 2 for every paper height up to 75, so the split is a property of the model and not of the exact height; Lily# cut 4 + 2 until the FOURTH divergence was found. ⚠️ ABOVE that plateau the two sides stop being comparable, and the reason is structural rather than arithmetic: at 76 and 77 LilyPond does not fit six systems onto one page, it RE-BREAKS the music into FIVE systems and puts those on one page (measured on a single-book probe: one SVG, 25 staff lines). LILYPOND-REF: lily/optimal-page-breaking.cc:139-173 -- Optimal_page_breaking::solve sweeps sys_count DOWNWARD from the line breaker's ideal, runs the full page spacing for every line-division configuration at each count, and keeps the global argmin of demerits; the page result therefore CHOOSES the line breaking. Lily# breaks lines once and pages afterwards, so that answer is unreachable for it at any spacing accuracy. Lily#'s own six-on-one-page threshold is 77 against LilyPond's 78 -- one staff space -- but do not read that as 'nearly right': the 76-77 window is a different shape of output, not a rounding. Keep this entry at 70 where both sides are in the same regime. It was not in the rod, and not in any of the three formulas ported before it: it was the ORPHAN PENALTY, charged on a condition LilyPond does not have. LilyPond spends orphan_penalty() only when lines_[page_start].last_markup_line_ or lines_[page_start-1].first_markup_line_ is set (page-spacing.cc:375-383) -- a multi-line markup PARAGRAPH split across a page boundary. Those flags come from a markup line's Prob (constrained-breaking.cc:633-636) and a music system's Line_details leaves both false with nothing ever setting them (constrained-breaking.hh:115-116), so music can never trigger it. Lily# was charging it for 'a lone system on the last page', which is exactly the shape of LilyPond's own 5 + 1, at 100000 against force-squared demerits of about 0.001 -- so that one invented condition decided every page break by itself. The old code cited page-breaking.cc:269 for it, which is where the VALUE is read from paper, not where it is applied: a LILYPOND-REF beside a formula is not evidence that the formula matches it (HANDOFF 5.2.1 (1)). Read with page.tight.page-count, which stayed exact throughout: the pair now agrees with LilyPond on both the number of pages and where the cut falls.

page.clef.first-staff-refpoint.why: Was +0.012727149; the clef is now seeded into the vertical skylines and it closes to -0.000082769. The seeded prediction was exact to the digit, and closing it needed a SECOND defect fixed: LayoutEngine's single-page path added SystemSpacing * 0.5 = 4 as the inter-system padding where LilyPond's system-system-spacing uses 1, so the clef's ink bound a spring LilyPond leaves at basic-distance. The remaining -8e-05 is the same LILC-vs-skyline sliver as system.clef-bounded-distance carries; see there. Original entry follows. Book S is book J's music moved inside the staff (b' on the middle line, up-stem stopping 3.5 above it) so that NOTHING hangs below the middle line and the deepest ink on every system is the CLEF. LilyPond's clef is an ordinary inside-staff grob and joins the staff's vertical skyline, reaching 3.540 below the refpoint, so it sets last-bottom-spacing's floor and through it the page's force. Lily#'s SkylineBuilder never seeds a clef at all -- it seeds the staff lines, notes, rests, accidentals, ledgers, dynamics and articulations -- so its deepest ink here should be the staff's own bottom line, 2.000000. PREDICTION, from Lily#'s own chain with the last spring blocked at padding 1 + 2.000000 = 3.000000: f = 4.628268/726 = 0.00637500, hence a first refpoint of 11.728801 (residual +0.012727) and a gap of 12.382500. Book W cannot catch this: its lowest notehead reaches 3.545, five thousandths PAST the clef, so W reads correct even with no clef in the skyline. Confirmed by measuring book S twice on 2.26.0, once with these notes and once with rests down to a 128th (glyph bottom 3.05 below the middle line): both give the identical 11.716074 and 12.255229, which is only possible if a third grob is setting them.

staff.staff.upper-note-to-lower-lines.why: EXACT. Was -0.050000, closed by seeding the staff lines as INK, and the prediction was exact both times -- seeded at -0.050000 before the change and landing on 0. THE STAFF SYMBOL'S EXTENT: Lily# seeded the staff lines at their CENTRE (+/-2.0, SkylineBuilder.SeedStaffSymbol) where LilyPond's skyline carries their INK (+/-2.05, half of the 0.1 line thickness past the centre). Asked of the grob itself, probes/glyph-skyline.ly reports StaffSymbol ext AND vertical-skylines both as (-2.05 . 2.05), so this is not an inference. SEEDED BEFORE THE CHANGE (HANDOFF 5.3) and the prediction was exact: -0.050000 measured against -0.050000 predicted. Align_interface spaces adjacent staves at max(skyline-distance + padding, minimum-distance, basic-distance) with StaffGrouper's 9 / 7 / 1 (align-interface.cc:228-238, define-grobs.scm:3352-3355), and the score is shaped so the LINES bind: the treble staff's d hangs 6 spaces below its middle line and its head reaches 0.545 further, while the same written pitch is the bass staff's own middle line, so nothing there rises above its top line. LilyPond 6.545 + 2.05 + 1 = 9.595000; Lily# 6.545 + 2.0 + 1 = 9.545000. Why the corpus could not see this before: every other entry is a SINGLE-staff score, and between two systems the staff lines lose to basic-distance 12 -- so nothing measured the staff symbol at all, and a fix to it moved 14 multi-staff fixtures and zero ledger points. PREDICTION: 0 when the seed becomes the ink.

staff.staff.dynamic-under-whole-note.why: CLOSED to -0.000076, and the prediction written before the change was exact to the digit. THREE defects had to go at once, because two of them carry opposite signs and neither could be judged alone: (1) THE PHANTOM STEM -- DynamicEngraver.GetLowestExtent returned noteY - DefaultStemLength for any down-stemmed note with no duration test, so a whole note reserved a stem it does not have; guarded on GetNoteValueFromFraction(...) >= 2, LILYPOND-REF lily/stem.cc Stem::is_normal_stem (duration-log >= 1); worth -3.000000. (2) THE HEAD'S OWN EXTENT, still the nominal +/-0.5 box in this engraver where the skyline had already moved to the glyph's LILC ink +/-0.545 (22120764); +0.045000. (3) THE DYNAMIC'S VERTICAL FOOTPRINT, 2.100000 against LilyPond's 3.188076; +1.088076. The three sum to -1.866924 and land the entry on -0.000076000 against -0.000076 predicted. THE FOOTPRINT IS NOW READ FROM THE FONT, per dynamic, because LilyPond's is: DynamicText is TEXT (scm/define-grobs.scm:1438 font-encoding fetaText, :1445 stencil ly:text-interface::print, :1449 Y-extent from stencil), so its extent is the drawn glyphs' own ink and differs between dynamics -- p descends below its baseline, m does not -- and no nominal constant can be right for all of them. Lily# had THREE of them for that one quantity (DynamicEngraver 0.64, OutsideStaffStacker 0.3, SkylineBuilder 0.3) and the answer to 'which is right' is none. ⚠️ THE INK COMES FROM THE OUTLINE, NOT FROM LILC, and that follows from the call path rather than from a fitted number: LILC is read only by get_indexed_char_dimensions (lily/open-type-font.cc:372-409), the GLYPH path, while a text stencil goes through Modified_font_metric::text_stencil (lily/modified-font-metric.cc:125-143) to Pango over the FreeType outline. The two are far apart -- LILC f is (-0.5834 . 2.0066) where the outline is (-0.692 . 1.896) -- so this is the opposite choice from ec7a2254 for the same reason ec7a2254 made its own. Confirmed, not derived, on three independent letter sets: \p reports (-0.584004 . 1.168008) and \mp reports (-0.584004 . 1.196016), the union of the OUTLINE p and m and unreachable from LILC. THE REMAINING -0.000076 IS PANGO'S QUANTISATION of that outline: LilyPond's skyline for the f glyph is 2.588076 tall against the outline's 2.588000, and closing it would need Pango, which Lily# does not have -- the same shape of named residual as the clef's LILC-versus-skyline sliver. A FOURTH defect was found in the same formula but is NOT in this number, because here the note binds and the staff does not: Lily# spent staff-padding 0.1 + padding 0.6 off the staff line CENTRES, where side-position-interface.cc:323-330 enters the staff as its EXTENT (+/-2.05) and :433-453 applies staff-padding as a FLOOR on the grob's own refpoint, never as a second padding. Those two errors cancelled to within 0.002, which is how DynamicPlacementTests' forced-up clearance -- pinned to LilyPond's own 1.342 -- passed for so long at two decimals; it is asserted at three now and decomposes only under the ported formula (2.05 + 0.6 + 0.692002). Original entry follows. MEASURED. ⚠️ THE PREDICTION WAS +2.955 AND THE ANSWER IS +1.866924 -- the sign is right and the magnitude is not, which by this entry's own terms means DO NOT go and fix GetLowestExtent yet. The gap formula is confirmed exact by its siblings P and Q (skyline distance + padding 1 when it beats basic-distance 9), so both sides decompose cleanly: LilyPond's upper staff reaches 10.783076 - 1 - 2.05 = 7.733076 below its refpoint, Lily#'s reaches 12.650000 - 1 - 2.05 = 9.600000. The note centre is -4.0 on both. Lily# claims a bottom of 7.5 (4.0 + the phantom 3.5) and LilyPond 4.545 (4.0 + the notehead's LILC ink), so the dynamic itself adds 2.100000 in Lily# and 3.188076 in LilyPond. TWO divergences of OPPOSITE sign therefore live in this one number: the phantom stem, +2.955, and the dynamic's own vertical footprint, -1.088076. Fixing only the first lands the entry near -1.088 rather than 0, and because the absolute value would shrink it would look like progress. ⚠️ The second half is now MEASURED, not inferred: probes/glyph-skyline.ly interrogates DynamicText and DynamicLineSpanner on this exact music and reports DynamicLineSpanner yoff=-6.441074 ext=(-1.292002 . 1.296021), so its bottom is -7.733076 -- the same 7.733076 the subtraction above produced, to the digit. It divides as padding 0.600053 from the notehead ink down to the spanner's TOP (scm/define-grobs.scm:1408 DynamicLineSpanner padding 0.6) plus the spanner's own height 2.588023, which is the `f` glyph's INK (DynamicText ext (-0.692002 . 1.896021), offset -0.6 inside the spanner). Lily# spends 0.6 + DynamicTextAscent 1.2 + DynamicTextDescent 0.3 = 2.1, i.e. it treats the glyph as 1.5 tall where LilyPond's f is 2.588. ⚠️ So the answer to 'which of Lily#'s two descents is right, OutsideStaffStacker's 0.3 or DynamicEngraver.cs:85's 0.64' is NEITHER -- LilyPond's f descends 0.692 and ascends 1.896, and since those are one glyph's ink they must differ per dynamic (p has a descender, m does not). A nominal constant cannot be right here at all; the fix is the same move 22120764 made for the notehead and ec7a2254 for X, namely read the ink from the font. GlyphMetricsGenerated.cs carries no dynamics glyphs today, so that means teaching Extract-EmmentalerMetrics.py to emit them. SEEDED BEFORE ANY FIX; the original prediction and its reasoning follow. The first ledger point that reaches DynamicEngraver. Suspicion, confirmed in the code but never measured: GetLowestExtent returns `noteY - DefaultStemLength` for any down-stemmed note with NO duration test, so a whole note reserves a stem it does not have. Identical to the defect 89aaa29f removed from SkylineBuilder, which branches on GetNoteValueFromFraction(...) >= 2 citing lily/stem.cc Stem::is_normal_stem. LilyPond draws no stem here either (duration-log 0), so its `a` reaches only its notehead's 0.545 below the centre at -4.0; Lily# reserves 3.5 from the same centre. PREDICTION: Lily# reads about 2.955 LARGER (3.5 against 0.545), i.e. residual near +2.955, because the dynamic hangs from whichever depth the note claims and the gap is bound by the dynamic on both sides (LilyPond's 10.783076 is comfortably past StaffGrouper's basic-distance of 9, so both sides are measuring the same thing rather than sitting on that floor). The sign is certain; the exact magnitude is not, because this entry also bundles any difference in where the two put a dynamic relative to the ink above it, and Lily#'s NoteheadHalfHeight is still the nominal 0.5 rather than the LILC 0.545 -- so a residual near 2.955 confirms the phantom stem dominates, and a residual far from it means something else is in the chain and must be found before touching GetLowestExtent.

staff.staff.lower-note-to-upper-lines.why: EXACT, in the two steps it was predicted to take: +1.450000 -> -0.050000 when the phantom stem went (landing on EXACTLY what the entry above read, which is what said the two scores then differed only by the staff symbol) -> 0 when the staff lines became ink. A PHANTOM STEM, and this entry is why the pair was worth writing. It is the other side of the same staff symbol as the entry above -- that one binds the LOWER staff's TOP line against ink coming down, this one binds the UPPER staff's BOTTOM line against ink going up -- and b' is the treble staff's middle line while sitting 6 spaces above the bass staff's, so LilyPond prints the same 9.595000 for both books and the two residuals were predicted to be identical. They are not: -0.050000 there, +1.450000 here. The difference is exactly a stem. SkylineBuilder.AddNoteBoxToSkylines gives EVERY notehead a stem of DefaultStemLength 3.5, and its own comment says 'quarter notes and shorter; half/whole have no stem' while the code that follows has no test of the duration at all.
